description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:262-269 — the rustdoc 'Caveats' section explicitly says: 'this entry point assumes the issuer cert IS the cert whose SubjectPublicKeyInfo the log committed to via issuer_key_hash. RFC 6962 §3.1 also allows Precertificate Signing Certificates [...] Detecting the delegated case is the caller's responsibility.'

That's currently documented but not enforced or detected. Callers using verify_embedded_scts also inherit this assumption (verify.rs:367-370 forwards it), but verify_embedded_scts is a tempting one-call API: 'how many SCTs in this cert verify?' Users naturally pass it (leaf, issuer-of-leaf) without checking whether the issuer is itself a Precert Signing Certificate.

The PSC case is detectable: a PSC has EKU 1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.4 (id-kp-CertificateTransparency) per RFC 6962 §3.1. The verifier could automatically detect it and walk one cert further up the chain. Today it can't.

Plausible failure: a CA delegates pre-cert submission to a PSC intermediate. Site operator runs verify_embedded_scts(leaf, immediate_issuer) where immediate_issuer is the PSC. Every SCT fails because the log committed to grandparent_issuer's SPKI, not immediate_issuer's. Returns Ok(0) — silently zero valid SCTs. Operator can't tell why.

Suggested fix: detect EKU id-kp-CertificateTransparency in the issuer cert and surface a new Error variant (PrecertSigningCertNotSupported) so the caller knows their input is wrong and needs to pass the PSC's issuer instead. Or extend the API to take a chain. Document explicitly that verify_embedded_scts works incorrectly for PSC-issued certs.
title: verify_sct_for_precert assumes immediate issuer signed the precert — no Precert Signing Certificate (PSC) handling
